KGaA (CGM) is a large German healthcare IT company headquartered in Koblenz, Germany. It is one of the world's largest e-health companies, with EUR 1.15 billion in 2024 revenue, over 8,700 employees globally, presence in 19 countries, and products used in 60 countries by more than 1.6 million users (physicians, dentists, pharmacists, healthcare institutions). The company was founded in 1987 by Frank Gotthardt and originally focused on dental information systems before expanding broadly. CGM delisted from the stock exchange in June 2025 after CVC Capital Partners took a ~28% stake.\n     9→\n    10→CGM's US operations (CompuGroup Medical US) are headquartered in Austin, Texas. The US business grew significantly through the **acquisition of eMDs in November 2020 for $240 million**. eMDs itself had previously been acquired by Marlin Equity Partners in 2015, and under Marlin's ownership had consolidated several ambulatory EHR products: it acquired McKesson's ambulatory software portfolio (Medisoft, Lytec, Practice Partner) in 2016 and Aprima Medical Software in 2019. By the time CGM acquired eMDs, the combined entity served 60,000+ providers across 32,000+ facilities in 70+ medical specialties with approximately 1,400 employees.\n    11→\n    12→Today, CGM US offers a portfolio of EHR and practice management products (CGM APRIMA, CGM eMDs, CGM CLINICAL, CGM ENTERPRISE EHR, CGM PLUS, CGM PRACTICE PARTNER), laboratory information systems (CGM LABDAQ, CGM MEDICUS, CGM SCHUYLAB), billing/RCM services (ARIA, eMEDIX clearinghouse), telehealth (CGM ELVI), and AI documentation (CGM AMBI). CGM positions itself as a top-4 provider in the US ambulatory information systems market.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: CGM eMDs\n    15→\n    16→CHPL ID: 11133\n    17→CHPL Product Number: 15.04.04.2700.eMDs.10.02.1.221227\n    18→Version: v10\n    19→Certification Date: 2022-12-27\n    20→Certification Body: Drummond Group\n    21→\n    22→### What It Is\n    23→\n    24→CGM eMDs (formerly \"e-MDs Solution Series\") is an **integrated EHR and practice management suite** designed for ambulatory/outpatient medical practices. It was originally created in 1996 by Dr. David Winn and a group of family practitioners in Austin, Texas, with a philosophy of being \"designed by physicians, for physicians.\" It was one of the first six ambulatory systems certified by CCHIT in 2007 and has historically received strong rankings in AAFP Family Practice Management surveys.\n    25→\n    26→The product is a single certified module that encompasses clinical charting, e-prescribing, scheduling, practice management, billing, and patient engagement. It is not a component of a larger product — it is itself the full product, though it integrates with several CGM add-on products and services (eMEDIX clearinghouse, ARIA RCM services, CGM AMBI ambient AI, CGM PAY payment processing, CGM CONNECTION patient communications).\n    27→\n    28→The product is certified across 28 ONC criteria covering clinical documentation (a)(1)-(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14)-(a)(15); transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(3); patient access (e)(3); public health reporting (f)(1), (f)(5); FHIR APIs (g)(7), (g)(9)-(g)(10); and EHI export (b)(10). This is a broadly certified product.\n    29→\n    30→### Users & Market\n    31→\n    32→**Target users**: Providers and clinical support staff (per CHPL listing). In practice, the system is used by physicians, nurses, medical assistants, front desk staff, billing staff, and practice managers.\n    33→\n    34→**Clinical settings**: Small to medium ambulatory practices primarily, but also supports larger multi-site organizations, Community Health Centers (CHCs), Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), Rural Health Clinics (RHCs), and Patient-Centered Medical Homes (PCMHs).\n    35→\n    36→**Specialties**: Supports 70+ medical specialties with customizable templates. Strong in primary care, family medicine, internal medicine, cardiology, dermatology, podiatry, OB/GYN, nephrology, and others. Includes a dedicated OB module.\n    37→\n    38→**Scale**: At the time of the CGM acquisition (2020), eMDs served 60,000+ providers in 32,000+ facilities. the how to extract and read the patient information included in the exported\nElectronic Health Information (EHI) zip file generated using CGM eMDs.\n\nGuide to your Electronic Health Information (EHI)\nYou have been provided an Electronic Health Information (EHI) export containing the files, records, and\nimages kept by your provider. The data is compressed in a .zip file named <Patient(lastname,\nfirstname[Account Number]) Date and time file was created.zip that must be extracted to view the\ncontents.\nFor example, the name of the .zip file created on November 28, 2023 at 3:31pm for Dupree Deptford with\nthe Account Number of DEPDUP0001, would be Patient(Deptford, Dupree[DEPDUP0001]) 2023‐11‐28 15‐\n31‐14.zip\n\nExtract the .zip file data\nMost current computer and phone operating systems (OS) can natively process compressed (.zip) files. If\nyour OS does not have the extraction functionality, you can download an application such as WinZip to\nperform the operation.\n\nWindows\n1. On your PC, go to the location containing the .zip file.\n2. Right‐click on the .zip file and then click Extract All.\n3. In the Enter password window, enter the password you were provided.\n4. On the Select a Destination and Extract Files window, browse to the location where the files will be\nextracted, and then click Extract.\n\nMacintosh\n1. On your Mac, go to the location containing the .zip file.\n2. Double‐click the .zip file.\n3. Enter the password you were provided. The files are extracted in the same folder as the .zip file.\n\nFolders, files, and images\nThe EHI data included in the .zip file depends on the data maintained and exported by your provider or\npractice. A list of the possible data included in the .zip file is shown in the tables below. of Contents\n\nElectronic Health Information Export User Guide for CGM eMDs\n2\n\nDecember 2023\n\n\fChapter 1 ‐ Electronic Health Information Export User\nGuide for CGM eMDs\nThis document describes the how to extract and read the patient information included in the exported\nElectronic Health Information (EHI) zip file generated using CGM eMDs.\n\nGuide to your Electronic Health Information (EHI)\nYou have been provided an Electronic Health Information (EHI) export containing the files, records, and\nimages kept by your provider. The data is compressed in a .zip file named <Patient(lastname,\nfirstname[Account Number]) Date and time file was created.zip that must be extracted to view the\ncontents.\nFor example, the name of the .zip file created on November 28, 2023 at 3:31pm for Dupree Deptford with\nthe Account Number of DEPDUP0001, would be Patient(Deptford, Dupree[DEPDUP0001]) 2023‐11‐28 15‐\n31‐14.zip\n\nExtract the .zip file data\nMost current computer and phone operating systems (OS) can natively process compressed (.zip) files. If\nyour OS does not have the extraction functionality, you can download an application such as WinZip to\nperform the operation.\n\nWindows\n1. On your PC, go to the location containing the .zip file.\n2. Right‐click on the .zip file and then click Extract All.\n3. In the Enter password window, enter the password you were provided.\n4. On the Select a Destination and Extract Files window, browse to the location where the files will be\nextracted, and then click Extract.\n\nMacintosh\n1. On your Mac, go to the location containing the .zip file.\n2. Double‐click the .zip file.\n3. Enter the password you were provided. The files are extracted in the same folder as the .zip file.\n\nFolders, files, and images\nThe EHI data included in the .zip file depends on the data maintained and exported by your provider or\npractice. A list of the possible data included in the .zip file is shown in the tables below. Introduction\nThis guide is intended to describe the available resources and capabilities of CGM’s FHIR API\nimplementation for eMDs and Aprima.\nThe API supports the following standards versions:\n• United States Core Data for Interoperability (USCDI) version 1\n• US Core 4.0 (FHIR US Core 4.0 Profile)\n• SMART App Launch 2.0.0\n• Bulk Data 1.0.1\nBelow you will find information on the following topics:\n\nTopic\n\nSee page\n\nHow do I register\n\n1\n\nSecurity overview\n\n2\n\nAPI Syntax\n\n2\n\nGeneral Search Information\n\n3\n\nResources\n\n5\n\nUSCDI Element to FHIR Resource Crosswalk\n\n65\n\nBinary and Attachments\n\n70\n\nBulk Data\n\n70\n\nService Base URL\n\n71\n\nContact Us\n\n71\n\nII. How do I register\n1. Please contact your account executive with your request.\n2. Reply to any questions that are required to complete the registration.\n3. Once we have reviewed your information and verified the customer's purchase of the FHIR\nAPI connector, we'll work with you and your vendor to connect the FHIR application with your\nEHR.\n\nFHIR API Documentation Guide\nApril 2024\n\n1\n\n\fSecurity overview\n\nIII. Security overview\nCGM’s FHIR implementation uses the SMART on FHIR authorization framework. More information\non the SMART on FHIR authorization framework and OAUTH 2.0 can be found at:\n\nSMART App Launch 2.0.0\nOAUTH 2.0\nThe SMART App Launch Framework connects third-party applications to Electronic Health Record\ndata, allowing apps to launch from inside or outside the user interface of an EHR system. It\nprovides a reliable, secure authorization protocol for a variety of app architectures, including apps\nthat run on an end-user's device as well as apps that run from an EHR. We support both\nstandalone and EHR launched apps for use by clinicians and healthcare providers. Standalone\napps are supported for patients, so\n• We support standalone and EHR launched apps\n• Standalone apps are supported for all users.\n• EHR launched apps are supported for clinicians and healthcare providers.\nCGM FHIR Server conforms to the Smart App Launch Framework 2.0.0. For further details on\nmaking authorization requests, and gaining access to FHIR resources, review the information at\nhttp://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/1.0.0/\nNote: The launch/patient scope is only available for standalone patient apps at this time. For\npractitioner apps, EHR Launch is the only manner in which context can be established.\nIf you want to set up your Client for access to multiple ApI Resources, an aud= must be passed as\npart of your access token request.\n\nIV. API Syntax\nCGM’s FHIR APIs support POST and GET calls to retrieve resources. For Bulk Data export\nDELETE is supported to delete a bulk data request that has been made.\nExamples:\nGET [base]/AllergyIntolerance?patient=123\n\nPOST [base]/AllergyIntolerace\nContent-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded\n\npatient=123\n\nFHIR API Documentation Guide\n2\n\nApril 2024\n\n\fGeneral Search Information\n\nV. General Search Information\nRegarding searches:\nNote on search nomenclature: In the examples, {system} is a component that can be omitted from\nthe search string to search across all systems for the provided identifier. Inclusion of {System}\nproduces a more targeted search.\nWhen system is omitted for a code/token search, search all of the potential systems for the query\nvalue.\nTo search by reference, see the following page: http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/search.html#reference\nTo search by dates, see the following page: http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/search.html#date\nFor more detailed information, see the following page: http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/search.html\n\nVI. Exception and Error Handling\nA. General\n1. Invalid/Not implemented resource returns “HTTP 404 – Unknown.”\n2. Only GET and POST are supported (not HTTP GET/POST) returns “HTTP 405 - Method Not\nAllowed.”\n3. No DB Connection Info Available (client not found in client discovery) returns “HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.”\n4. No available workers returns “HTTP 503 - Not Available.”\n5. Invalid JSON returned from DB (details added in diagnostics) returns “500 - Internal Server\nError.”\n\nEX:\n{\n\"resourceType\": \"OperationOutcome\",\n\"text\": {\n\"status\": \"generated\"\n},\n\"issue\": [\n{\n\"severity\": \"error\",\n\"code\": \"processing\",\n\"diagnostics\": \"The resource could not be generated ‐ Error ‐ DB ERROR ‐\nConversion failed when converting from a character string to\nuniqueidentifier.\"\n}\n]\n\nFHIR API Documentation Guide\nApril 2024\n\n3\n\n\fSearch\n\n}\n6. Read Interactions\n1. NULL or empty response returns “500 – Internal Server Error” for invalid JSON\n\nB. Search\n1. If an unrecognized search term is passed, the system will attempt to execute the search\nwithout that parameter included. This may result in larger result sets than intended.\n2. Empty bundle response (no results returned) returns “200 – OK.”\n\nC. Bulk Data\n1. Failed Delete (output contains ERROR): Could Not DELETE Resource 500\n2. Status check on deleted resource: 404 Could not provide status - Resource $requestId has\nbeen deleted\n3. General status check error/no valid status: 404 – Not Found\n4. $export general error: 500 Could not generate the $export request\n5. Empty output for ndjson: 500 Fetched Resource has no data\n\nD. Authentication\n1. Authentication for CGM Identity conforms to the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) RFC\n6749 OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework.\n2. Token Not Provided (no client found/no token returned) returns “401 – Unauthorized.”\n3. Auth error is not null from Introspection returns “403 – Forbidden.”\n\nif {$_active != \"true\"} {\nset authError \"Token Not Valid ‐ Token Not Active\"\n} elseif {$_nbf > $now} {\nset authError \"Token Not Valid ‐ Token Too New\"\n} elseif {$_exp < $now} {\nset authError \"Token Not Valid ‐ Expired Token\"\n} elseif {[lsearch $_aud $audience] < 0} {\nset authError \"Token Not Valid ‐ Invalid Audience ‐ $audience\"\n} elseif {![regexp \"$_iss\" $::introspect_api_uri]} {\nset authError \"Token Not Valid ‐ Invalid Issuer\"\n} elseif {!$isScopeValid} {\nset authError \"Token Not Valid ‐ Invalid Scope\"\n}\n\nFHIR API Documentation Guide\n4\n\nApril 2024\n\n\fResources\n\nVII. DiagnosticReport\nSummary\nThis resource includes both Laboratory Report and Report and Note Exchange.\nLaboratory Report: Laboratory results are grouped and summarized using the\nDiagnosticReport resource which typically reference Observation resource(s). Each\nObservation resource represents an individual laboratory test and result value or component\nresult values, or a “nested” panel (such as a microbial susceptibility panel) which references\nother observations. They can also be presented in report form or as free text. The\nDiagnosticReport resource records, searches, and fetches laboratory results associated with a\n\nFHIR API Documentation Guide\n16\n\nApril 2024\n\n\fFields--Laboratory\n\npatient. DocumentReference\nSummary\nThis profile sets minimum expectations for searching and fetching patient documents including\nClinical Notes using the DocumentReference resource. It identifies the mandatory core\nelements, extensions, vocabularies and value sets that shall be present in the\nDocumentReference resource when using this profile.\nA reference to a document of any kind for any purpose. Provides metadata about the\ndocument so that the document can be discovered and managed. The scope of a document is\nany serialized object with a mime-type, so includes formal patient centric documents (CDA),\nclinical notes, scanned paper, and non-patient specific documents like policy Observation\nSummary\nThe observation resource combines the Lab Results, Vitals, and Smoking resources. Each\nObservation resource represents an individual laboratory test and result value, a “nested”\npanel (such as a microbial susceptibility panel) which references other observations, or rarely\na laboratory test with component result values. The Vital Signs profile sets minimum\nexpectations for the Observation resource to record, search and fetch the vital signs\nassociated with a patient that include the primary vital signs plus additional measurements\nsuch as height, weight and BMI. The Observation resource records, searches, and fetches\nsmoking status data associated with a patient.\n\nFHIR API Documentation Guide\n38\n\nApril 2024\n\n\fFields\n\nFields\nName\n\nUsed in CGM Bundles and Paging\nIf you’re searching for resources, the results will be returned in a bundle. A bundle has some\ninformation about the search overall, as well as the resources that met the criteria.\nOnly a set amount of resources will be returned in a bundle. If the number of resources that met\nthe search criteria exceeds that number, the returned resources will be spread out over multiple\npages of results. There’s information at the top of bundle that tells you what you’re currently\nlooking at (self link), where the previous page is, and where the next page is. To get all resources\nthat met your search criteria, you’ll need to continue making requests using the next page url until\nyou get to the end of the search set.\nIf you’re on the first page of results, there won’t be a previous link. If you’re on the last page of\nresults, there will be no next link.\nIf you’ve asked for provenance information with your search, each page of results will have both the\nresource and provenance records for those resources.\n\nX. Binary and Attachments\nRather than making page sizes very small for DiagnosticReport and DocumentReference\nresources, we’ve opted to present attachment data as a link to a Binary resource. Searches should\nbe executed against the DiagnosticReport and DocumentReference resources to locate the\ndocuments you’d like to obtain. Once you know which document you want to request, you can call\nthe Binary url to obtain it.\n\nXI. Bulk Data\nCGM’s FHIR implementation for Aprima and eMDs supports group compartment bulk data\nsearches for back-end systems. More information about FHIR Bulk Data Access and Backend\nServices Authorization can be found at http://hl7.org/fhir/uv/bulkdata/STU1.0.1/\nIf you’re implementing a back-end system that intends to use group-export, first identify which\nGroup you’d like to pull data against.\nBulk Export calls are initiated by calling the $export operation for the desired Group:\nEx. GET [base]/Group/<GroupID>/$export\nBulk Data export is an asynchronous request. Once the request has been submitted, you’ll be\nreturned a url to check on the status of the request. Until the request has been completed, this url\nwill simply indicate that the job is in progress. Once complete it will return a manifest that contains\nlinks to new line delimited json files (ndjson) for all qualifying resources that your application has\nbeen scoped for, as well as any errors that occurred .\nThe NDJSON files require an access token to retrieve.\n\nFHIR API Documentation Guide\n68\n\nApril 2024\n\n\fService Base URL\n\nIf you want to cancel your bulk data request, you can post a delete to the status url that you were\nprovided\nEx. DEL [base]/Group/{GroupID}/$export/request-status/{RequestID}\nOperations\n$export – Exports all clinical data for the specified group that your application has been scoped\nfor. At this time CGM FHIR APIs do not support _type filtering.\nGET [base]/Group/<GroupID>/$export\n\nXII. Service Base URL\nA list of CGM customers that have enabled FHIR APIs can be found at https://\nidentity.emdscloud.com/api/api-resource/fhir.\nInformation from this url is presented as JSON with DisplayName, Description, and the customer’s\nbase url.\n\nEx.\n{\n\"DisplayName\" : \"The Burn Unit\",\n\"Description\" : \"A clinic that’s on FHIR\",\n\"ResourceURL\" : \"https://myclinicurl.cgm.com/fhir/api”\n}\n\nXIII. Just simplifying and synchronizing your healthcare operations.</p><p>&nbsp;</p><p><br>&nbsp;</p></div></div></div></div></div><div class=\"two-column container-fluid background--white\" id><div class=\"container\"><div class=\"row \"><div class=\"col-12 col-lg-6\"><div class=\"two-column__left neos-contentcollection\"><div id=\"case-study\" data-anchor=\"true\" class=\"headline headline--normal container--content-flow\"><h2>CGM eMDs boosts revenues, cuts costs for Alaska practice</h2></div><div class=\"text container--content-flow\" id><p>Mario Lanza, MD, knew that he needed an electronic health record when he started a family practice in Anchorage, Alaska, in 2006. Tight Integrations. The Best Options for CGM eMDs</h2></div><div class=\"text-grid container\" id><h2></h2><div class=\"text-grid__items neos-contentcollection\"><div class=\"text-grid-item\"><a><span class=\"icon-container\"><div class=\"icon lazyload icon--size-xl\" data-iconuri=\"https://www.cgm.com/_Resources/Static/Packages/Cgm.CgmCom/Assets/Icons/Custom/icon-target-group-patient-communication.svg?bust=21077c3d\"></div></span></a><div class=\"text-grid-item__content\"><div class=\"text-grid-item__content__text\"><h3>Patient Relationship Management&nbsp;</h3><p>Manage your patient communication automatically. The fully integrated <a href=\"/usa_en/products/electronic-health-records/patient-engagement/cgm-connection.html\"><strong>CGM CONNECTION</strong></a> tool is a state-of-the-art text, email, and phone communication option for CGM eMDs. Send appointment reminders and step up your marketing and clinical engagement with blast messaging for promotions, birthday messages, announcements, and more.</p></div></div></div><div class=\"text-grid-item\"><a><span class=\"icon-container\"><div class=\"icon lazyload icon--size-xl\" data-iconuri=\"https://www.cgm.com/_Resources/Static/Packages/Cgm.CgmCom/Assets/Icons/Custom/icon-target-group-doctor.svg?bust=de7f2fb8\"></div></span></a><div class=\"text-grid-item__content\"><div class=\"text-grid-item__content__text\"><h3>CGM AMBI Ambient AI</h3><p>Maximize face-to-face time with your patients using ambient AI. CGM AMBI listens to an entire patient encounter, parsing out and transcribing information from the doctor, nurse, patient, and supporting family members. <a href=\"/usa_en/products/electronic-health-records/ai-solutions-for-your-ehr/cgm-ambi.html\"><strong>CGM AMBI</strong></a> enters information into the different parts of the patient note and suggests diagnoses, orders, and billing codes.</p></div></div></div><div class=\"text-grid-item\"><a><span class=\"icon-container\"><div class=\"icon lazyload icon--size-xl\" data-iconuri=\"https://www.cgm.com/_Resources/Static/Packages/Cgm.CgmCom/Assets/Icons/Custom/icon-target-group-hardware.svg?bust=459b2087\"></div></span></a><div class=\"text-grid-item__content\"><div class=\"text-grid-item__content__text\"><h3>Integrated EDI &amp; Statements</h3><p>Our <a href=\"/usa_en/products/billing-services-edi/emedix-healthcare-edi-claims-clearinghouse.html\"><strong>eMEDIX</strong></a> clearinghouse means you have a totally integrated practice management and claims management system. Real-time eligibility, ERA posting, advanced edits and scrubbing, claim status automation, and denial management and analysis tools are unmatched, saving staff time and optimizing revenues. You can also leverage integrated statements that offer print along with text and email notifications, delivering a better patient experience to help accelerate payments.</p></div></div></div><div class=\"text-grid-item\"><a><span class=\"icon-container\"><div class=\"icon lazyload icon--size-xl\" data-iconuri=\"https://www.cgm.com/_Resources/Static/Packages/Cgm.CgmCom/Assets/Icons/Custom/icon-cgm-sozial-dienstplan.svg?bust=4476f7b7\"></div></span></a><div class=\"text-grid-item__content\"><div class=\"text-grid-item__content__text\"><h3>eCQM Reporting</h3><p><a href=\"/usa_en/products/electronic-health-records/mips-dashboard/cgm-measures.html\"><strong>CGM MEASURES</strong></a> for CGM eMDs is an integrated application that lets you dynamically monitor your scoring for the CMS Merit-Based Incentive Payment System (MIPS). Our proven electronic clinical quality measures (eCQM) reporting tool makes it easier to manage quality and report performance.</p></div></div></div><div class=\"text-grid-item\"><a><span class=\"icon-container\"><div class=\"icon lazyload icon--size-xl\" data-iconuri=\"https://www.cgm.com/_Resources/Static/Packages/Cgm.CgmCom/Assets/Icons/Custom/icon-challenge-icons-billing-cgm.svg?bust=9a873337\"></div></span></a><div class=\"text-grid-item__content\"><div class=\"text-grid-item__content__text\"><h3>Integrated Payments</h3><p><a href=\"/usa_en/products/practice-management-software/payment-solutions/cgm-pay.html\"><strong>CGM PAY</strong></a> delivers a fully integrated method to boost in-office payments, reduce past-due accounts, and prevent future delinquencies. Use advanced card-on-file capabilities and automated payment plans to create a patient-friendly approach that enables practices to move from \"past due\" to \"paid.\"</p></div></div></div><div class=\"text-grid-item\"><a><span class=\"icon-container\"><div class=\"icon lazyload icon--size-xl\" data-iconuri=\"https://www.cgm.com/_Resources/Static/Packages/Cgm.CgmCom/Assets/Icons/Ion/bar-chart-outline.svg?bust=681d9ee7\"></div></span></a><div class=\"text-grid-item__content\"><div class=\"text-grid-item__content__text\"><h3>Revenue Cycle Services</h3><p>Our 3x KLAS award-winning <a href=\"/usa_en/products/billing-services-edi/aria-rcm-services.html\"><strong>ARIA RCM Services</strong></a> can help you, whether it is filling staffing gaps, working your aging AR, or complete end-to-end services. Choose the services that benefit you the most, so you can keep your focus on patient care.</p></div></div></div><div class=\"text-grid-item\"><a><span class=\"icon-container\"><div class=\"icon lazyload icon--size-xl\" data-iconuri=\"https://www.cgm.com/_Resources/Static/Packages/Cgm.CgmCom/Assets/Icons/Custom/icon-target-group-hospital.svg?bust=7696ca83\"></div></span></a><div class=\"text-grid-item__content\"><div class=\"text-grid-item__content__text\"><h3>Hosting&nbsp;</h3><p>Shift your focus away from the demands of IT and back to your patients by hosting CGM eMDs on a CGM cloud server. Enjoy the same functionality, access, and support without worrying about limitations, demands, and costs of maintaining your servers and database onsite.</p></div></div></div><div class=\"text-grid-item\"><a><span class=\"icon-container\"><div class=\"icon lazyload icon--size-xl\" data-iconuri=\"https://www.cgm.com/_Resources/Static/Packages/Cgm.CgmCom/Assets/Icons/Custom/icon-challenge-icons-integration.svg?bust=2ebc168c\"></div></span></a><div class=\"text-grid-item__content\"><div class=\"text-grid-item__content__text\"><h3>Interoperability</h3><p>Share information to smart apps, health systems, population health platforms, and more. The flexibility of CGM eMDs means compatibility with FHIR and other secure, API interfaces. Connect to the Surescripts RLE health information exchange or the CommonWell Health Alliance Services network to improve care coordination, lower costs, and more.</p></div></div></div><div class=\"text-grid-item\"><a><span class=\"icon-container\"><div class=\"icon lazyload icon--size-xl\" data-iconuri=\"https://www.cgm.com/_Resources/Static/Packages/Cgm.CgmCom/Assets/Icons/Custom/icon-challenge-icons-electronic-scripts.svg?bust=ea79fff2\"></div></span></a><div class=\"text-grid-item__content\"><div class=\"text-grid-item__content__text\"><h3>Prescribing</h3><p>Prescribing is a huge part of an EHR. CGM PRESCRIBE, winner of many Surescripts White Coat Awards, is THE standard for prescription management. New, refill, changed meds. Easy. Patient information handouts and a free app that improves adherence.
